content.title: About
content.content: Stewed goat, Puerto Rican style is a traditional island dish made from tender pieces of goat meat slowly simmered in a fragrant sauce of tomatoes, paprika, garlic, onion, olive oil, and characteristic Puerto Rican spices such as adobo and cumin.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Goat meat is considered a delicacy in Puerto Rico and is often served at family celebrations.
Long, low‑heat cooking makes the meat exceptionally tender and flavorful.
The sauce traditionally includes a hint of “piri‑piri” heat typical of Caribbean cuisine.
The dish is commonly accompanied by rice, beans, and fried plantains.
Fresh herbs like oregano and cilantro are added for a bright aromatic note.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Goat meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Lower fat content
items.content: Compared with beef, goat meat generally contains less saturated fat, making it a heart‑friendlier option.

items.title: Rich in iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals support immune function and healthy blood.

items.title: B‑vitamins source
items.content: Goat meat is a good source of vitamin B12 and niacin, which aid nerve health and metabolism.

items.title: Benefits from spices
items.content: Adobo, cumin, and garlic have antioxidant and anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to goat meat, experiencing skin rashes or digestive reactions.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improper cooking can lead to salmonella or campylobacter contamination.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Traditional sauces are often salty; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Caution with liver disease
items.content: Goat meat is relatively high in purines, which can raise uric acid levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the stew hot, typically with boiled rice, beans, and fried plantains. The meat can be shredded for tacos, burritos, or used as a filling for pies.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly to at least 75 °C before serving.
